images.title: Poste de développement — lumière du jour
images.prompt: Use case: compositing. Create one polished photorealistic editorial photograph for a French Unity game developer's LinkedIn portfolio. Landscape composition 3:2, high resolution, one complete photograph, not a collage or contact sheet. Input image 1 is actual project gameplay content and must appear on a large monitor as faithfully as possible, preserving the exact pixel-art protagonist, green and orange scenery, platforms, coins and HUD; input image 2 is an actual wide overview of the same level and may be visible on a secondary smaller monitor. Show a believable modest individual development desk, black monitor, ordinary keyboard and mouse, notebook, warm wood, daylight from a window, tactile materials and natural slight imperfections. Photograph at desk height with a gentle three-quarter angle, 35mm editorial photography, restrained contrast, crisp main screen, calm professional atmosphere. No people, no faces, no implied real studio or team, no futuristic interface, no RGB neon gaming room, no awards, no performance graphs, no invented 3D game or new level content. Include a discreet but clearly readable bottom caption in a clean sans-serif: 'ILLUSTRATION IA'. Include a small clear 'UNITY / C#' at the top. This is openly an illustrative staged workspace, not a documentary photograph or an actual screenshot of the user's office. Do not add any further marketing text.

images.title: Du contrôleur C# au gameplay
images.prompt: Use case: compositing. Produce one refined photorealistic close-up photograph of a small Unity 2D game development workstation for LinkedIn, landscape 3:2, high resolution. The supplied image is exact real gameplay from the user's prototype; faithfully place it on an external monitor as content, preserving the red-shirted pixel-art character, green/orange pixel landscape, platforms, coins and score HUD without redesigning the game. In the foreground show a laptop or adjacent screen displaying a sober dark C# code editor with only these real lines legible: 'public float coyoteTime = 0.12f;' and 'public float jumpBufferTime = 0.12f;' and the file tab 'PlayerController.cs'. Code should look typeset and plausible, not an invented full IDE screenshot or fake Unity Profiler. Focus on the relationship of code to game, attractive diagonal composition, subtle screen reflections, soft daylight, realistic black hardware and neutral desk, documentary-like materials with no people. Keep the screens sharp enough to see their content. Avoid neon, sci-fi, fake metrics, logos of studios, trophies, fabricated professional achievements. Include the small exact title 'DU CODE AU GAMEPLAY' and a clearly readable bottom caption 'ILLUSTRATION IA'. One finished image only, no collage, no multiple options.

No people, no hands, no invented office identity, no brand names, no fake FPS or performance data, no prototype features that are not in the references. Keep the authentic level print as the visual focus, with readable silhouettes and faithful layout. Include a small exact title 'CONSTRUIRE LE PARCOURS' and a clearly readable bottom caption 'ILLUSTRATION IA'.
